text.p: Shares in Belgian chemicals and plastics group Tessenderlo Chemie outperformed the wider market on Wednesday, gaining 0.9 percent, after the company said it hoped profits would reach 1995's record level.
"It is a nice reaction by Tessenderlo, although volumes are thin," a trader said. "Tessenderlo's prospects for 1997 are quite good," another said.

The stock was up 150 francs at 17,650 at 1045 GMT after Tessenderlo said on Tuesday it expected earnings to continue to improve this year, but it was unlikely the 30 percent growth rate of the first quarter would be seen for the year as a whole.

Board chairman Gerard Marchand told shareholders, "It is not certain today that we will achieve the record result of 1995 this year, but running the risk of being over-optimistic, I call upon you to share this hope with me."

Pre-tax profits rose by about 30 percent in the first quarter to 892 million Belgian francs, representing a recovery from 1996 when pre-tax profit dropped to 3.69 billion from 3.84 billion in 1995 in what the company called a depressed economic environment.
Generale Bank said in a stock comment on Wednesday it rated the share a 'strong hold'.
Generale said that reaching the 1995 profit level largely depended on a further recovery of PVC prices, "probably after the traditionally weak summer months."

"Regarding future growth initiatives more opportunities are seen in the plastics converting sector than in final chemicals...the plastics converting sector might well become Tessenderlo's largest division by the end of the year," it said.

Bank BBL brokerage Vermeulen Raemdonck, rating the share a 'hold', said it was hard to forecast earnings since it was unclear how "intense" the summer weakness would be and when new capacities would come on stream.
It said, "We consider the share as fairly valued and even slightly overvalued."
